questions.q: The three major types of learning described by ____ psychology are classical conditioning, operant conditioning and observational learning.
questions.explanation: Behavioral psychology focuses on observable learning and identifies classical conditioning, operant conditioning and observational learning as its three major types.

questions.q: According to the view of Watson, psychology is ____.
options: about internal mental processes that cannot be measured and observed
questions.explanation: Watson argued psychology should be a purely objective, experimental branch of natural science aimed at predicting and controlling behavior. He rejected subjective introspection and the study of unobservable mental processes.
Pavlov discovered classical conditioning through his work with dogs salivating to a neutral stimulus paired with food. Operant conditioning is associated with Skinner.

questions.q: The process by which organisms learn to respond to certain stimuli but not to others is known as ____.
questions.explanation: Stimulus discrimination is learning to respond only to the conditioned stimulus and not to similar stimuli. Stimulus generalization is the opposite, responding to stimuli similar to the conditioned stimulus.

questions.q: Higher-order conditioning is intrinsically weaker than its first-order counterpart.
questions.explanation: In higher-order conditioning a new neutral stimulus is paired with an already conditioned stimulus rather than the unconditioned stimulus, so the resulting response is weaker and extinguishes more easily.

questions.q: ____ is the process of gradually changing the quality of a response.
questions.explanation: Shaping reinforces successive approximations of a target behavior, gradually changing the response until the desired behavior is reached. Modeling involves learning by observing others.

questions.q: The works of ____ were instrumental in engendering the dramatic shift from behaviorism to cognitive theories.
questions.explanation: Tolman's cognitive maps, Piaget's theory of cognitive development and the German Gestalt psychologists' work on insight and perception all emphasized internal mental processes, helping drive the shift to cognitive theories.

questions.q: ____ intelligence is the ability to perceive the visual-spatial world accurately and involves sensitivity to color, line, shape, form, space, and the potential for recognizing and manipulating the patterns of spaces.
questions.explanation: In Gardner's theory of multiple intelligences, spatial intelligence is the ability to perceive and manipulate visual-spatial information, as seen in artists, architects and navigators.

questions.q: Sternberg proposed his theory in 1985 as an alternative to the idea of the ____.
questions.explanation: Sternberg's triarchic theory (analytical, creative and practical intelligence) was proposed as an alternative to Spearman's single general intelligence factor (g).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a kind of product in the structure of intellect model?
questions.explanation: In Guilford's structure of intellect model, the products are units, classes, relations, systems, transformations and implications. Symbolic is a type of content, not a product.
